# The core journeys

What people do with Faro end to end, and the checks that drive it (`npm run evals`; `[evals/journeys.cjs](../../evals/journeys.cjs)`). Journeys and checks a module owns are in its own section ([Metric library](../modules/metrics/README.md), [Spreadsheets](../modules/spreadsheets/README.md)). Who the journeys are for: `docs/journeys.md`.

## Journeys

Each drives the built app in Chromium as a person would, on a phone (390px) and a desktop (1440px), and is scored on the ten-point ease test below. `budget` is the most steps it may take.

## Platform checks

Checks run across every screen: design rules, widths, motion, errors.

| Id | Check | Requirements | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Animation switches off under reduced motion | `MOTION` | `evals/journeys.cjs` |
| P2 | Loading shows a skeleton, and an unreachable database becomes a clear error with Try again | `MOTION` `NO-ERRORS` | `evals/journeys.cjs` |
| P6 | Design rules on every screen: no coloured edges, accent bars, glyph icons, gradients, glass or state capsules, and every status shape beside its own word | `DESIGN-RULES` `SHAPE-MATCHES-WORD` | `evals/journeys.cjs` |
| P7 | Wide screens and a short laptop: nothing clipped, each kind of page uses the room it has, and a goal’s chart is above the fold | `WIDE-SCREENS` | `evals/journeys.cjs` |
| P8 | The goals start in the first screen: the Goals header stays short on a phone and a desktop | `WIDE-SCREENS` `PHONE` | `evals/journeys.cjs` |
| P9 | Every width from a small phone to an ultra-wide monitor: no sideways scroll, nothing cut off, navigation always there, prose a readable width | `EVERY-WIDTH` | `evals/journeys.cjs` |
| P10 | Fit and finish: text follows the browser’s size, one control height, phone tables and toolbars that stack, a usable rail, no sideways scroll, one left edge | `FIT-AND-FINISH` | `evals/journeys.cjs` |
| P15 | A comment in the demo survives a reload, only the saves are stored, and a browser that refuses says so | `DEMO-STORAGE` | `evals/journeys.cjs` |

## The ease test

Every journey is scored out of ten, one point each:

- `entry`: Starts from the person's home, with the way in visible without scrolling
- `one-action`: Every step shows exactly one primary action
- `progress`: The person can see how far along they are (ring, steps or count)
- `budget`: Done within the interaction budget for the journey
- `errors`: An incomplete step says what's missing, in place, instead of failing silently
- `finish`: Finishing is confirmed, with the next thing offered
- `attention`: Anything off track, stale or slipping in the journey is flagged with its reason
- `parity`: The same journey completes on a 390px phone and a 1440px desktop
- `a11y`: No serious accessibility issues; primary buttons are at least 44px tall on a phone
- `logged`: The change it makes is in the change log with who, when and before → after

## Not built yet, on purpose

- Dependencies between goals
- Jira context
- Slack check-in cards and reminders
- AI coaching on a draft (beta)
- Sign-in and per-person permissions
- Data integrations (Power BI, Grafana, ServiceNow)
